I’ve read the full transcript of **Pints with Aquinas episode 601**, with **Fr Anthony Mourad of St George and St Anthony Coptic Orthodox Church in Ottawa**, and saved **53 claims and arguments** with timestamps and follow-up sources.

The strongest parts to investigate are:

- **1:07–1:10 and 1:37–1:41:** the figure reportedly remained luminous after electricity was cut, and searches reportedly found no projection equipment.
- **1:13–1:18:** named church investigators reportedly saw the appearances themselves; a medical committee investigated healing claims.
- **1:21–1:23:** Mourad relays his father’s eyewitness account of a wheelchair user standing after prayer.
- **1:32–1:33:** Benedictine **Jerome Palmer’s 1969 investigation** provides a route toward records much closer to the events.

**This is a considerably stronger argument than simply pointing to a luminous photograph.** It combines repeated sightings, reported interventions against a hoax, and medical claims.

A particularly promising lead is photographer **Wagih Rizk Matta**: the archive reproduces a named physician’s account of restored elbow movement after serious injury. I located the transcription; the signed report’s image still needs examination. [Testimony and medical report](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/eyewitness/waguih-rizk-matta/)

messages.text:
**We now have contemporary documentary support for the lights-out account and a reproduced signed medical report for one healing.**

**The power cutoff:** I retrieved and inspected all six Arabic pages of the report signed **30 April 1968 by William Farid Basili, Director of Inquiries and Complaints at Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism**. Page 3 describes searchlights being directed at the figure, nearby lamps being smashed, and **all the area’s lights being extinguished while the figure remained visible**. This account predates the podcast by decades. [Ministry report and scans](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/ministry-of-tourism-department-of-inquiries/)

The precise wording establishes a reported lights-out intervention. It does **not** specify the later five-kilometre boundary, hours-long duration, or provide utility switching records. *Watani’s* 5 May account repeats the sequence, apparently drawing on the same Ministry narrative.

**Matta’s arm:** I found the signed report attributed to **Dr Zarif Bishara Rizk, FRCS, MRCOG, consultant surgeon at Manchiet El Bakry Hospital in Cairo**. It describes Matta’s severe June 1967 elbow injury, subsequent restricted movement, and later practically full flexion and extension—which the surgeon says he cannot medically explain. [Medical account](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/eyewitness/waguih-rizk-matta/)

The original adds treatment details omitted from shorter retellings: attempted surgical repair, plaster and antibiotics. Those details belong in our assessment. The report supports unexpectedly restored function; Matta’s testimony supplies the connection to photographing the apparition.

**The other healings:** The 1969 committee booklet contains eight named cases. These include bladder cancer treated by **Dr Aziz Fam, identified there as a Cairo University urology professor**, plus thyroid disease, paralysis and other conditions. I found summaries, rather than complete signed hospital files, for those cases. [Committee booklet](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/st-marys-apparitions/)

A **2 June 1968 Watani** transcription also reproduces dated examinations and describes collecting prior records and referring patients to specialists. That supports an active contemporary medical investigation, although this translation still needs checking against the Arabic clinical passages. [Newspaper report](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/fr/newspaper/watani-june-21968/)

I saved the scans and registered **11 named healing cases**, distinguishing signed reports, published examinations and narrative summaries: [full findings and medical-record audit](research/zeitoun-investigation-records-20261027/findings-and-medical-records.txt).

messages.text:
**You’ve captured the central reported case, including details that a “people saw a vague light” summary would leave unanswered.** The records describe a recognizable female figure, movement, changes of orientation, bowing toward the cross, blessing gestures, and luminous dove-like forms. The investigators themselves reported several of these observations. [Committee report](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/report-of-the-committee-formed-by-his-holiness-the-pope-to-verify-the-authenticity-of-the-apparitions-of-the-virgin-mary/)

I would refine three points:

- **Appearance count:** Mourad gives **94**, and later compilations give approximately **90–95**, rather than 80. The contemporary Ministry report records **27 by 30 April 1968**. We haven’t audited the complete three-year register. [Count and references](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/skeptic/the-allegation-of-myth/)
- **Government acknowledgment:** Yes—the Ministry’s signed report affirmatively presents the appearances as miraculous. That is stronger than merely acknowledging crowds. Its April 1968 conclusion, however, cannot itself certify every subsequent appearance across three years. [Government report](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/ministry-of-tourism-department-of-inquiries/)
- **Facial clarity:** Some witnesses describe eyes, nose, mouth and detailed clothing; others explicitly say distance prevented distinguishing features. “Some observers reported recognizable facial detail” accurately preserves the stronger testimony without attributing it to everyone. [Zeinab Taher’s account](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/eyewitness/zeinab-taher-2/), [Vivian Goubran’s account](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/eyewitness/vivian-sami-goubran/)

The main things missing from your summary are:

- **The reported persistence after surrounding lights were extinguished.**
- **The healing claims and medical investigation**, including the signed Matta report we recovered.
- **Some prolonged appearances:** the patriarchal statement describes periods exceeding two hours.
- **Silence:** no spoken message was reported, despite the apparently purposeful gestures. [Patriarchal statement](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/statement-by-the-coptic-orthodox-patriarch/)

And yes, the predominantly Muslim setting and Muslim witnesses matter. Shared Muslim reverence for Mary is relevant context, but it doesn’t erase their testimony about a figure reportedly bowing before a **Christian cross**. That religiously specific behavior belongs in the argument alongside the light, movement, repetition and healings.

messages.text:
**I haven’t reached “the supernatural is more likely than not” yet. But Zeitoun gives me substantial reason to consider that conclusion.**

Repeated public appearances, Muslim and Christian witnesses, descriptions of purposeful movement and bowing before a cross, governmental acknowledgment, the lights-out account, and medically attested recoveries create a real explanatory burden. Simply saying “suggestion,” “hysteria,” or “a projection” does not adequately answer that combined case.

What still holds me back is the distance between the strongest claims and what we have directly verified. For example, Matta’s signed report establishes a surgeon’s judgment that restored movement was medically unexplained; the connection to an instantaneous recovery during the apparition comes through testimony. The blackout report is substantial contemporary evidence, but it leaves important details about illumination and observation unspecified.

Those limitations reduce how confidently I can infer the cause. **They do not make the affirmative evidence disappear.**

You are also right about accumulation: Fátima and Zeitoun cannot each be assigned zero weight merely because each remains disputed. Their combined evidence can rationally change the assessment of supernatural Christianity. One sufficiently established event could cross that threshold; there is no requirement to produce an endless succession of miracles.

messages.text:
**Zeitoun’s public apparition is a serious positive case for a supernatural event. My earlier response did not adequately confront your argument.**

Here is what gives it weight:

- **The investigators claimed to see it themselves.** The three priests appointed by Coptic Pope Kyrillos VI reported interviewing the initial witnesses, then watching on subsequent nights. They described a complete luminous figure moving above the domes, bowing before the cross and blessing the crowd, alongside luminous dove-like forms. That is considerably more specific than people interpreting an unidentified glow. [Committee report, April 30, 1968](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/report-of-the-committee-formed-by-his-holiness-the-pope-to-verify-the-authenticity-of-the-apparitions-of-the-virgin-mary/).
- **There is contemporary governmental affirmation.** William Farid Basili, director of inquiries and complaints at Egypt’s Ministry of Tourism, presented the appearances as genuine and described Muslim and Christian witnesses. His report says nearby lamps were broken and all lights in the area extinguished, while the figure remained visible. This is meaningful evidence against an ordinary reflection from those lights. [Basili’s report, April 30, 1968](https://ourladyofzeitoun.com/en/report/ministry-of-tourism-department-of-inquiries/).
- **The combination matters:** repeated appearances, public visibility, movement, religiously specific gestures and witnesses across religious boundaries. An explanation has to address that combination. Simply saying “crowds can misinterpret things” does not accomplish that.

**The main gap now is connecting the strongest reports to particular, dated appearances.** We already have substantial testimony; the next gains come from examining it more closely.

The most useful information would be:

1. **Detailed records of a few especially clear appearances.** Who saw the full figure, for how long, from which positions, and what movements did they independently describe? We already have reports of movement, blessing and bowing toward the cross; matching accounts from the same night would strengthen that evidence.

2. **The original investigation’s procedures.** Who inspected the roof and surrounding buildings? What possible sources of illumination did they check? What exactly was disconnected, and did the same appearance continue afterward? The existing government report and Nelson’s observations give us a foundation.

3. **Original photographs with provenance.** Photographer, date, negative or earliest print, exposure information if available, and whether an image was retouched. That would let us assess what the photographs independently establish.

4. **The earlier sources behind later scholarship.** Bullivant’s 1970 account and DeVincenzo’s 1988 overview are useful targets, particularly for their witness references. For Nasser specifically, we still need the original Fawzi passage and its supporting source.

The question we should press is: **does any ordinary explanation adequately account for the best documented appearances—including their reported recognizable form, movement, duration and viewing conditions?** Cultural context alone doesn’t answer that.
